itens.t: Defeated Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro flees to the US via Argentina and Ecuador
itens.r: Following his defeat in the presidential election to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and an order by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes to surrender his passports, conservative Senator Flávio Bolsonaro fled Brazil. He crossed into Argentina on Tuesday night before immediately boarding a private flight to Guayaquil, Ecuador, and eventually heading to the United States. President Lula sharply criticized the departure as shameful, while political analysts noted it has thrown the Brazilian right into a fierce leadership contest. Meanwhile, U.S. President Donald Trump remarked that he would approve Bolsonaro's entry and criticized the Brazilian election results.
itens.d:
Defeated presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro entered Argentina from Brazil via the Tancredo Neves International Bridge accompanied by his wife and daughters. Official immigration authorities confirmed that the group presented valid travel documents without legal impediments.

Shortly after crossing the border, the family boarded a private flight operated by Baires Fly S.A. bound for Guayaquil, Ecuador. The entire transit through Argentina was registered by application authorities without any reported incidents.

itens.t: Israel Faces Political Stalemate as Vote Count Nears Completion in Parliamentary Election
itens.r: With more than half of the votes tallied in Israel's parliamentary election, projections indicate a deadlocked race with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc holding a narrow lead but falling short of a clear majority. Opposition leaders Gadi Eisenkot and Yair Lapid claimed the results signaled a strong mandate for change from voters tired of the incumbent government. Concurrently, Arab parties achieved historic turnout and are projected to secure a record number of seats in the Knesset.
itens.d:
More than half of the votes in Israel's parliamentary election have been counted, according to the Central Election Committee. Updated projections indicate that parties supporting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu are extending their lead but remain short of an absolute majority.

With 51 percent of the votes tallied, Netanyahu's Likud party led with nearly 21 percent, while the opposition Yashar party trailed behind. Projections suggest Netanyahu's bloc could secure 55 seats in the Knesset, remaining below the 61 seats required for majority control.
